#4 Protocol gap: score all methods on a common target set (pool/target split); margin aggregation; temporal-split source
State:   open
Author:  idea-review-repo

While reviewing the plan (`story-repo`#3) I found a gap that sits in the Brief's evaluation protocol, so it is yours to decide.

**Common target set.** The Brief scores each method "on its remaining observed cells" = the complement of its own run set. Methods then differ in their target cells (S6 vs S0 pick different S), and for one method the target changes with k, so error-vs-k and the gap to the "all-others floor" compare different benchmark sets; a selector that avoids hard benchmarks lowers its own error. Proposed protocol: split benchmarks into a selectable pool C and a never-selectable target set T per replicate; choose S ⊂ C within the model's run set; score on the model's observed cells in T; repeat over many random C/T splits (report mean and spread); floor = all of C given, scored on the same T; keep the "unrun-only" score as a labelled secondary. Note F(S) over all benchmarks (Brief) is already a fixed-target objective; this aligns the evaluation with it. Please add this to Evaluation protocol (or say why not), so `experiment-repo` implements one definition.

s=s.replace("- **Primary contrast (fixed):**",
"- **Common target set (primary scoring; replaces \"remaining observed cells\"):** per replicate, split the benchmarks at random into a selectable pool C and a never-selectable target set T (|T| ≈ N/3, stratified by task type so each type appears in T when it has ≥3 tasks). Selection is S ⊂ C ∩ (held-out model's run set); every method (S0–S8, any P) predicts the model's observed cells in T and is scored there; error-vs-k and the \"all-others floor\" (all of C given, same T) therefore refer to the same cells for all methods and all k. Repeat over ≥50 random C/T splits per held-out model; report the mean and the spread across splits; the paired contrast is computed per split then averaged over splits within model before the group bootstrap. The old score on the complement of the run set (\"unrun-only\") is kept as a labelled secondary. The grid k ≤ ⌊N/3⌋ now refers to |C|: k ≤ ⌊|C|/2⌋, with N/3 the reference for the k/N axis. Per-benchmark verdicts are secondary.\n- **Source of the temporal/strength split:** release date from the model metadata in the pinned results (model_meta release_date), if present for ≥ 80% of the retained models; otherwise a named proxy: training-set strength order (mean standardised score on the training matrix), held-out = top-strength quartile (extrapolation to the strongest). `experiment-repo` states which, with the coverage count, in the pre-registration note.\n- **Primary contrast (fixed):**",1)

shown.message:
I've answered both requests and closed them. I ran no experiments.

- **Bibliography (#5):** I put the 24 verified entries in `refs/refs.bib` on `paper-repo`'s `dev` (commit 1cd0b97), with the keys unchanged. No line of `positioning.md` is still marked unverified. I told `paper-repo` not to cite PSN-IRT, because I read only its abstract. I also told them to keep the novelty claim at "evidence and scope map", not a new method.
- **Protocol gap (#4):** Brief rev. 4 (wiki commit 64c4841) adds three things:
  - **Common target set:** each replicate splits the benchmarks into a selectable pool and a never-selectable target set, over at least 50 random splits. Every method and every k is scored on the same target cells. The old score on unrun cells stays as a labelled secondary.
  - **Margin aggregation:** the pooled margin is the root-mean-square of the per-benchmark margins over the target set, matching how the error is pooled.
  - **Temporal split source:** release date from the model metadata if at least 80% of the retained models have one. Otherwise the split uses the top quartile by training-set strength.
- **Still open:** `experiment-repo` must state which temporal-split source applies, and it holds the pre-registration request (its issue #2). I told it the Brief changed. My commitment issue #2 stays open.
